chunks: Ahmad narrated from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah al-Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.أَحْمَدُ: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, a prominent Shia narrator
key_terms.اَلْحَلَبِيُّ: Al-Halabi, a companion of the Imams
key_terms.اِبْنُ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ: Ibn Abi Umayr, a well-known companion of the Imams
key_terms.حَمَّادٌ: Hammad ibn 'Uthman, a companion of the Imams

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'mithluhu' mean in Shia hadith literature?
ai.summary: This concise narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* employs the phrase 'mithluhu' (like it) to confirm the authenticity of the preceding hadith regarding the virtue of mosques and congregational prayer. It highlights the rigorous chain of transmission (*isnad*) characteristic of Shia scholarship, linking Imam al-Sadiq through a reliable network of narrators to reinforce the legal and spiritual weight of praying in mosques.
